sanskrit: tasmād dhatvākṛtaprajñaṃ lubdhaṃ kāmavaśānugam labhatāṃ pāṇḍavaḥ kāmaṃ dharme 'dharme 'pi vā kṛte
english: Therefore, now that this man of feeble wits, greedy and a slave to his desires, has been slain, let the Pāṇḍava have his heart's wish—whether what was done was righteous or unrighteous.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity ukte dharmarājena vāsudevo 'bravīd idam kāmam astv evam iti vai kṛcchrād yadukulodvahaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the King of Righteousness had spoken thus, Vāsudeva, the upholder of the Yadu line, said only with difficulty, "So be it; let it be as you wish."

sanskrit: ity ukto vāsudevena bhīmapriyahitaiṣiṇā anvamodata tat sarvaṃ yad bhīmena kṛtaṃ yudhi
english: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, who sought Bhīma's welfare and delight, Yudhiṣṭhira approved of all that Bhīma had done in the battle.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi hatvājau tava putram amarṣaṇaḥ abhivādyāgrataḥ sthitvā saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: And Bhīmasena, the wrathful one, having slain your son in battle, stood before Yudhiṣṭhira, saluted him, and, filled with joy, folded his palms in reverence.

sanskrit: provāca sumahātejā dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram harṣād utphullanayano jitakāśī viśāṃ pate
english: O lord of peoples, that hero of mighty splendour, his eyes wide with gladness and wearing the look of a victor, spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: tavādya pṛthivī rājan kṣemā nihatakaṇṭakā tāṃ praśādhi mahārāja svadharmam anupālayan
english: "Today the earth is yours, O king, made secure and freed of every thorn. Govern it, O great king, upholding your own sacred duty."

sanskrit: yas tu kartāsya vairasya nikṛtyā nikṛtipriyaḥ so 'yaṃ vinihataḥ śete pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate
english: "He who was the author of this enmity, the lover of deceit who delighted in treachery—he now lies slain upon the earth, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaprabhṛtayaḥ sarve te cogravādinaḥ rādheyaḥ śakuniś cāpi nihatās tava śatravaḥ
english: "Duḥśāsana and all the rest, those harsh of speech, Rādheya too, and Śakuni—all your foes have been struck down."

sanskrit: seyaṃ ratnasamākīrṇā mahī savanaparvatā upāvṛttā mahārāja tvām adya nihatadviṣam
english: "This earth, strewn with jewels, with its forests and its mountains, has this day returned to you, O great king, now that your enemies are slain."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gataṃ vairasya nidhanaṃ hato rājā suyodhanaḥ kṛṣṇasya matam āsthāya vijiteyaṃ vasuṃdharā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The end of the feud has come; King Suyodhana is slain. Following the counsel of Kṛṣṇa, this earth has been won.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā gatas tvam ānṛṇyaṃ mātuḥ kopasya cobhayoḥ diṣṭyā jayasi durdharṣa diṣṭyā śatrur nipātitaḥ
english: By good fortune you have discharged your debt both to our mother and to her wrath; by good fortune you are victorious, O unassailable one; by good fortune the enemy has been cast down.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca hataṃ duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenena saṃyuge pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayāś caiva kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When they beheld Duryodhana slain by Bhīmasena in the combat, what did the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas do, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hataṃ duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenena saṃyuge siṃheneva mahārāja mattaṃ vanagajaṃ vane
english: Saṃjaya said: When they beheld Duryodhana slain by Bhīmasena in the combat, O great king, as a lion slays a rutting wild elephant in the forest—

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamanasas tatra kṛṣṇena saha pāṇḍavāḥ pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayāś caiva nihate kurunandane
english: there, with their hearts rejoicing, the Pāṇḍavas together with Kṛṣṇa, and the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas, when the joy of the Kurus had been slain—

sanskrit: āvidhyann uttarīyāṇi siṃhanādāṃś ca nedire naitān harṣasamāviṣṭān iyaṃ sehe vasuṃdharā
english: whirled their upper garments and roared their lion-roars; so filled with joy were they that the earth itself could scarcely bear them.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣy anye vyākṣipanta jyāś cāpy anye tathākṣipan dadhmur anye mahāśaṅkhān anye jaghnuś ca dundubhīḥ
english: Some brandished their bows, and others twanged their bowstrings; some blew their great conches, and others beat their kettledrums.

sanskrit: cikrīḍuś ca tathaivānye jahasuś ca tavāhitāḥ abruvaṃś cāsakṛd vīrā bhīmasenam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Still others sported and laughed, those foes of yours, and again and again the heroes spoke these words to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ bhavatā karma raṇe 'dya sumahat kṛtam kauravendraṃ raṇe hatvā gadayātikṛtaśramam
english: "A hard deed, a very great deed, have you accomplished in battle this day, slaying with your mace the lord of the Kauravas, worn out as he was by his exertions."

sanskrit: indreṇeva hi vṛtrasya vadhaṃ paramasaṃyuge tvayā kṛtam amanyanta śatror vadham imaṃ janāḥ
english: As Indra slew Vṛtra in the supreme combat, so the people deemed this slaying of the foe to have been wrought by you.

sanskrit: carantaṃ vividhān mārgān maṇḍalāni ca sarvaśaḥ duryodhanam imaṃ śūraṃ ko 'nyo hanyād vṛkodarāt
english: "This brave Duryodhana, who ranged through manifold paths and wheeled in every circling movement—who other than Vṛkodara could have slain him?"

sanskrit: vairasya ca gataḥ pāraṃ tvam ihānyaiḥ sudurgamam aśakyam etad anyena saṃpādayitum īdṛśam
english: "You have reached the far shore of this enmity, a shore beyond the reach of others here; such a feat as this no other could have brought to pass."

sanskrit: kuñjareṇeva mattena vīra saṃgrāmamūrdhani duryodhanaśiro diṣṭyā pādena mṛditaṃ tvayā
english: "As by a rutting tusker, O hero, at the head of the fray, by good fortune Duryodhana's head has been crushed by your foot."

sanskrit: siṃhena mahiṣasyeva kṛtvā saṃgaram adbhutam duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ diṣṭyā pītaṃ tvayānagha
english: "As a lion does with a buffalo, having waged a wondrous battle, by good fortune the blood of Duḥśāsana was drunk by you, O blameless one."

sanskrit: ye viprakurvan rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram mūrdhni teṣāṃ kṛtaḥ pādo diṣṭyā te svena karmaṇā
english: "Those who wronged King Yudhiṣṭhira, the soul of righteousness—upon their heads, by your own deeds and by good fortune, your foot has been set."

sanskrit: amitrāṇām adhiṣṭhānād vadhād duryodhanasya ca bhīma diṣṭyā pṛthivyāṃ te prathitaṃ sumahad yaśaḥ
english: "By the overthrow of your enemies and by the slaying of Duryodhana, O Bhīma, by good fortune your vast renown is spread abroad over the earth."

sanskrit: evaṃ nūnaṃ hate vṛtre śakraṃ nandanti bandinaḥ tathā tvāṃ nihatāmitraṃ vayaṃ nandāma bhārata
english: "Surely, as the bards rejoiced over Śakra when Vṛtra was slain, so we rejoice over you, your foe destroyed, O descendant of Bharata."

sanskrit: duryodhanavadhe yāni romāṇi hṛṣitāni naḥ adyāpi na vihṛṣyanti tāni tad viddhi bhārata ity abruvan bhīmasenaṃ vātikās tatra saṃgatāḥ
english: "The hairs upon our bodies that bristled with joy at the slaying of Duryodhana—know, O descendant of Bharata, that even now they will not lie down again." So the praise-singers gathered there spoke to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tān hṛṣṭān puruṣavyāghrān pāñcālān pāṇḍavaiḥ saha bruvataḥ sadṛśaṃ tatra provāca madhusūdanaḥ
english: To those exultant tigers among men, the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, who spoke words befitting the moment, Madhusūdana then said:

sanskrit: na nyāyyaṃ nihataḥ śatrur bhūyo hantuṃ janādhipāḥ asakṛd vāgbhir ugrābhir nihato hy eṣa mandadhīḥ
english: "It is not fitting, O lords of men, to slay again and again an enemy already slain. This dullard has indeed already been struck down by your harsh words."

sanskrit: tadaivaiṣa hataḥ pāpo yadaiva nirapatrapaḥ lubdhaḥ pāpasahāyaś ca suhṛdāṃ śāsanātigaḥ
english: "This wicked man was slain at that very moment when, shameless, greedy, the companion of the wicked, he transgressed the counsel of his friends."

sanskrit: bahuśo viduradroṇakṛpagāṅgeyasṛñjayaiḥ pāṇḍubhyaḥ procyamāno 'pi pitryam aṃśaṃ na dattavān
english: "Though urged again and again by Vidura, Droṇa, Kṛpa, the son of Gaṅgā, and the Sṛñjayas, he would not grant the Pāṇḍavas their ancestral share."

sanskrit: naiṣa yogyo 'dya mitraṃ vā śatrur vā puruṣādhamaḥ kim anenātinunnena vāgbhiḥ kāṣṭhasadharmaṇā
english: "This basest of men is no longer fit to be reckoned friend or foe. What use is it to keep reviling with words one who has become as a senseless log of wood?"

sanskrit: ratheṣv ārohata kṣipraṃ gacchāmo vasudhādhipāḥ diṣṭyā hato 'yaṃ pāpātmā sāmātyajñātibāndhavaḥ
english: "Mount your chariots swiftly; let us depart, O lords of the earth. By good fortune this evil-souled one is slain, together with his counsellors, his kinsmen, and his allies."

sanskrit: iti śrutvā tv adhikṣepaṃ kṛṣṇād duryodhano nṛpaḥ amarṣavaśam āpanna udatiṣṭhad viśāṃ pate
english: But hearing this reproach from Kṛṣṇa, King Duryodhana, overcome with indignation, raised himself up, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sphigdeśenopaviṣṭaḥ sa dorbhyāṃ viṣṭabhya medinīm dṛṣṭiṃ bhrūsaṃkaṭāṃ kṛtvā vāsudeve nyapātayat
english: Seated upon his haunches, propping himself against the earth with both arms, he knit his brows into a frown and cast his gaze upon Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: ardhonnataśarīrasya rūpam āsīn nṛpasya tat kruddhasyāśīviṣasyeva cchinnapucchasya bhārata
english: The form of the king, his body half upraised, was then like that of an angered venomous serpent whose tail had been severed, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: prāṇāntakaraṇīṃ ghorāṃ vedanām avicintayan duryodhano vāsudevaṃ vāgbhir ugrābhir ārdayat
english: Heedless of the dreadful, life-ending agony, Duryodhana assailed Vāsudeva with savage words:

sanskrit: kaṃsadāsasya dāyāda na te lajjāsty anena vai adharmeṇa gadāyuddhe yad ahaṃ vinipātitaḥ
english: "O heir of the slave of Kaṃsa, have you no shame for this, that by unrighteous means I have been brought down in the mace-duel?"

sanskrit: ūrū bhindhīti bhīmasya smṛtiṃ mithyā prayacchatā kiṃ na vijñātam etan me yad arjunam avocathāḥ
english: "Do you think I did not perceive how, treacherously prompting Bhīma's memory, you said to Arjuna, 'Smash his thighs'?"

sanskrit: ghātayitvā mahīpālān ṛjuyuddhān sahasraśaḥ jihmair upāyair bahubhir na te lajjā na te ghṛṇā
english: "Having caused thousands of kings who fought fairly to be slain by many crooked devices—have you no shame, no remorse?"

sanskrit: ahany ahani śūrāṇāṃ kurvāṇaḥ kadanaṃ mahat śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya ghātitas te pitāmahaḥ
english: "Day after day, as he wrought great slaughter among heroes, your grandsire was made to be slain by you, with Śikhaṇḍin set in the forefront."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmnaḥ sanāmānaṃ hatvā nāgaṃ sudurmate ācāryo nyāsitaḥ śastraṃ kiṃ tan na viditaṃ mama
english: "By slaying the elephant that bore the same name as Aśvatthāman, O most wicked one, the preceptor was made to lay down his weapons—do you think this is unknown to me?"

sanskrit: sa cānena nṛśaṃsena dhṛṣṭadyumnena vīryavān pātyamānas tvayā dṛṣṭo na cainaṃ tvam avārayaḥ
english: "And when that valiant one was being struck down by this cruel Dhṛṣṭadyumna, you looked on and did not restrain him."

sanskrit: vadhārthaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya yācitāṃ śaktim eva ca ghaṭotkace vyaṃsayathāḥ kas tvattaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ
english: "The very spear that was begged for, meant for the slaying of the son of Pāṇḍu, you caused to be wasted upon Ghaṭotkaca. Who is a greater doer of evil than you?"

sanskrit: chinnabāhuḥ prāyagatas tathā bhūriśravā balī tvayā nisṛṣṭena hataḥ śaineyena durātmanā
english: "His arm severed, set upon the vow of fasting unto death, the mighty Bhūriśravas was slain at your bidding by the vile descendant of Śini."

sanskrit: kurvāṇaś cottamaṃ karma karṇaḥ pārthajigīṣayā vyaṃsanenāśvasenasya pannagendrasutasya vai
english: "And Karṇa, performing a deed of the highest valour in his longing to vanquish Pārtha, was thwarted through the wasting of the arrow that was Aśvasena, son of the lord of serpents—"

sanskrit: punaś ca patite cakre vyasanārtaḥ parājitaḥ pātitaḥ samare karṇaś cakravyagro 'graṇīr nṛṇām
english: "and again, when his chariot wheel sank down, that foremost of men, Karṇa, struck by calamity and overcome, distracted with his wheel, was cast down in the combat."

sanskrit: yadi māṃ cāpi karṇaṃ ca bhīṣmadroṇau ca saṃyuge ṛjunā pratiyudhyethā na te syād vijayo dhruvam
english: "Had you fought fairly against me and against Karṇa, against Bhīṣma and Droṇa in battle, victory would surely never have been yours."

sanskrit: tvayā punar anāryeṇa jihmamārgeṇa pārthivāḥ svadharmam anutiṣṭhanto vayaṃ cānye ca ghātitāḥ
english: "But by you, ignoble one, through crooked ways were we and other kings, who kept to our own sacred duty, brought to destruction."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca hatas tvam asi gāndhāre sabhrātṛsutabāndhavaḥ sagaṇaḥ sasuhṛc caiva pāpamārgam anuṣṭhitaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: O son of Gāndhārī, you have been slain together with your brothers, your sons, and your kinsmen, your followers and your friends, because you trod the path of wickedness.

sanskrit: tavaiva duṣkṛtair vīrau bhīṣmadroṇau nipātitau karṇaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye tava śīlānuvartakaḥ
english: It was by your own misdeeds that the heroes Bhīṣma and Droṇa were laid low, and Karṇa too, who followed your ways, was slain in the encounter.

sanskrit: yācyamāno mayā mūḍha pitryam aṃśaṃ na ditsasi pāṇḍavebhyaḥ svarājyārdhaṃ lobhāc chakuniniścayāt
english: Though entreated by me, O fool, you would not give the Pāṇḍavas their ancestral share, the half of their own kingdom, out of greed and at Śakuni's resolve.

sanskrit: viṣaṃ te bhīmasenāya dattaṃ sarve ca pāṇḍavāḥ pradīpitā jatugṛhe mātrā saha sudurmate
english: You administered poison to Bhīmasena, and all the Pāṇḍavas, together with their mother, you sought to burn in the house of lac, O most wicked one.

sanskrit: sabhāyāṃ yājñasenī ca kṛṣṭā dyūte rajasvalā tadaiva tāvad duṣṭātman vadhyas tvaṃ nirapatrapaḥ
english: And the daughter of Yajñasena, in her courses, was dragged into the assembly hall at the dicing—even then, O evil-souled and shameless one, you deserved to be killed.

sanskrit: anakṣajñaṃ ca dharmajñaṃ saubalenākṣavedinā nikṛtyā yat parājaiṣīs tasmād asi hato raṇe
english: Because, with the dice-cunning son of Subala, you by treachery defeated one who knew righteousness but knew nothing of the dice—for that you have been slain in battle.

sanskrit: jayadrathena pāpena yat kṛṣṇā kleśitā vane yāteṣu mṛgayāṃ teṣu tṛṇabindor athāśrame
english: Because, when they had gone hunting, Kṛṣṇā was tormented in the forest by the wicked Jayadratha at the hermitage of Tṛṇabindu—

sanskrit: abhimanyuś ca yad bāla eko bahubhir āhave tvaddoṣair nihataḥ pāpa tasmād asi hato raṇe
english: and because Abhimanyu, a mere boy, alone amid many in the fray, was slain through your misdeeds, O wicked one—for that you have been slain in battle.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca adhītaṃ vidhivad dattaṃ bhūḥ praśāstā sasāgarā mūrdhni sthitam amitrāṇāṃ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: Duryodhana said: I have studied as the rule prescribes, I have given gifts duly, I have ruled the earth with its girdling seas, I have stood upon the heads of my enemies—who then has come to a happier end than I?

sanskrit: yad iṣṭaṃ kṣatrabandhūnāṃ svadharmam anupaśyatām tad idaṃ nidhanaṃ prāptaṃ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: That very death which is the wish of warriors who keep their own sacred duty in view—that death I have now attained. Who then has come to a happier end than I?

sanskrit: devārhā mānuṣā bhogāḥ prāptā asulabhā nṛpaiḥ aiśvaryaṃ cottamaṃ prāptaṃ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: Pleasures worthy of the gods, such mortal joys as kings can scarcely win, I have enjoyed; sovereignty supreme I have attained. Who then has come to a happier end than I?

sanskrit: sasuhṛt sānubandhaś ca svargaṃ gantāham acyuta yūyaṃ vihatasaṃkalpāḥ śocanto vartayiṣyatha
english: With my friends and my followers I shall go to heaven, O Acyuta; while you, your purposes shattered, shall live on in grief.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca asya vākyasya nidhane kururājasya bhārata apatat sumahad varṣaṃ puṣpāṇāṃ puṇyagandhinām
english: Saṃjaya said: At the close of this speech of the king of the Kurus, O descendant of Bharata, a great shower of sweet-scented flowers fell down.

sanskrit: avādayanta gandharvā jaguś cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ siddhāś ca mumucur vācaḥ sādhu sādhv iti bhārata
english: The Gandharvas made music and the throngs of Apsarases sang, and the Siddhas uttered their voices, crying "Well done! Well done!", O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: vavau ca surabhir vāyuḥ puṇyagandho mṛduḥ sukhaḥ vyarājatāmalaṃ caiva nabho vaiḍūryasaṃnibham
english: And a fragrant breeze blew, holy-scented, gentle and pleasant, and the spotless sky shone forth, gleaming like a sapphire.

sanskrit: atyadbhutāni te dṛṣṭvā vāsudevapurogamāḥ duryodhanasya pūjāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā vrīḍām upāgaman
english: Beholding these wondrous portents, and seeing the honour shown to Duryodhana, those led by Vāsudeva were overcome with shame.

sanskrit: hatāṃś cādharmataḥ śrutvā śokārtāḥ śuśucur hi te bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ tathā karṇaṃ bhūriśravasam eva ca
english: And hearing that they had been slain unrighteously, they grieved, stricken with sorrow, for Bhīṣma and Droṇa, for Karṇa, and for Bhūriśravas.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu cintāparān dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavān dīnacetasaḥ provācedaṃ vacaḥ kṛṣṇo meghadundubhinisvanaḥ
english: But seeing the Pāṇḍavas sunk in thought and downcast in spirit, Kṛṣṇa, whose voice was as the thunder of the clouds, spoke these words:

sanskrit: naiṣa śakyo 'tiśīghrāstras te ca sarve mahārathāḥ ṛjuyuddhena vikrāntā hantuṃ yuṣmābhir āhave
english: "This swift-handed warrior, and all those great chariot-heroes, valiant as they were, could not have been slain by you in fair fight upon the field."

sanskrit: upāyā vihitā hy ete mayā tasmān narādhipāḥ anyathā pāṇḍaveyānāṃ nābhaviṣyaj jayaḥ kva cit
english: "These stratagems were therefore devised by me, O lords of men; otherwise the sons of Pāṇḍu would never anywhere have won the victory."

sanskrit: te hi sarve mahātmānaś catvāro 'tirathā bhuvi na śakyā dharmato hantuṃ lokapālair api svayam
english: "For those four great-souled warriors, mightiest of charioteers upon the earth, could not by righteous means have been slain even by the guardians of the worlds themselves."

sanskrit: tathaivāyaṃ gadāpāṇir dhārtarāṣṭro gataklamaḥ na śakyo dharmato hantuṃ kālenāpīha daṇḍinā
english: "And likewise this son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, mace in hand and unwearied, could not by righteous means have been slain even by Death himself, the wielder of the rod."

sanskrit: na ca vo hṛdi kartavyaṃ yad ayaṃ ghātito nṛpaḥ mithyāvadhyās tathopāyair bahavaḥ śatravo 'dhikāḥ
english: "Nor should you take it to heart that this king was struck down. When the enemies are many and overpowering, they must be slain by stratagem and craft."

sanskrit: pūrvair anugato mārgo devair asuraghātibhiḥ sadbhiś cānugataḥ panthāḥ sa sarvair anugamyate
english: "This is the path followed of old by the gods who slew the Asuras; the road that the good have trodden is the road that all men follow."

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyāḥ sma sāyāhne nivāsaṃ rocayāmahe sāśvanāgarathāḥ sarve viśramāmo narādhipāḥ
english: "Our task is accomplished; let us settle upon our lodging now in the evening. Let us all rest, O lords of men, with our horses, elephants, and chariots."

sanskrit: vāsudevavacaḥ śrutvā tadānīṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha pāñcālā bhṛśasaṃhṛṣṭā vineduḥ siṃhasaṃghavat
english: Hearing the words of Vāsudeva, the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, exceedingly gladdened, then roared like a pride of lions.

sanskrit: tataḥ prādhmāpayañ śaṅkhān pāñcajanyaṃ ca mādhavaḥ hṛṣṭā duryodhanaṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Then those bulls among men, rejoicing to see Duryodhana slain, blew their conches, and Mādhava blew the Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas te prayayuḥ sarve nivāsāya mahīkṣitaḥ śaṅkhān pradhmāpayanto vai hṛṣṭāḥ parighabāhavaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then all those rulers of the earth set forth toward their lodging, blowing their conches in their joy, their arms like iron bludgeons.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavān gacchataś cāpi śibiraṃ no viśāṃ pate maheṣvāso 'nvagāt paścād yuyutsuḥ sātyakis tathā
english: And as the Pāṇḍavas were going to our camp, O lord of peoples, the great archer Yuyutsu followed behind them, and Sātyaki as well.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ sarve cānye maheṣvāsā yayuḥ svaśibirāṇy uta
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, and the sons of Draupadī, one and all, and all the other great archers, went each to his own encampment.

sanskrit: tatas te prāviśan pārthā hatatviṭkaṃ hateśvaram duryodhanasya śibiraṃ raṅgavad visṛte jane
english: Then the sons of Pṛthā entered the camp of Duryodhana, its splendour quenched and its lord slain, like a theatre when the people have dispersed.
